questions.q: What specific question does data lineage answer that an ownership model or a systems-of-record map does not?
options: Who is accountable for a dataset
Which system should be treated as authoritative
How a specific value in a specific record came to be what it is, including every transformation along the way
What classification tier a dataset belongs to
questions.explain: Lineage traces the actual history of a value -- its origin and every transformation and movement since -- which is a different question from who owns the data or which system is authoritative.

questions.q: By default, how long is standard Salesforce Field History Tracking data guaranteed to be retained for orgs created after June 1, 2011?
options: 30 days
6 months
18 months
10 years
questions.explain: Standard Field History Tracking data is only guaranteed to be retained for 18 months for orgs created after June 1, 2011; extending retention beyond that requires Field Audit Trail, part of Salesforce Shield.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's Setup Audit Trail actually track, and what is its retention window?
options: Field-level before/after data values, retained indefinitely
Changes to metadata and configuration made in Setup (new permission sets, profile changes, automation changes), covering the last 180 days
Every API call made against the org, retained for 18 months
Customer data lineage across integrated external systems
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail logs changes to the org's own configuration and metadata, not data value changes, and covers only the last 180 days -- it is a metadata-change log, not a data-lineage tool.

questions.q: Why is cross-system lineage (e.g., tracing a value from an ERP, through middleware, into Salesforce) not automatic?
options: Because Salesforce blocks all external data imports
Because the receiving system has no way to know why a value arrived the way it did unless the integration was deliberately designed to preserve and expose that history
Because cross-system lineage is illegal under most data-privacy regulations
Because Field History Tracking automatically captures the full history of every external system
questions.explain: A value populated by an integration looks identical, from the receiving system's perspective, to one typed in by a user -- unless the integration was specifically built to record and expose the transformation history.

questions.q: Before deprecating a legacy system or changing a field's data type, lineage is primarily used for which purpose?
options: Impact analysis -- determining what downstream reports or systems depend on the data before touching it
Automatically rolling back the change if something breaks
Replacing the need for a documented systems-of-record map
Encrypting the field going forward
questions.explain: Lineage enables impact analysis: knowing what depends on a piece of data before you change or retire it, so 'nothing should break' is a verified claim rather than a guess.
